messages.subject: GEOM_BAR (Stacked Bar)
parts:
Dear Rexpert,

Although I was able to produce the plot (ggplot GEOM_BAR - stacked), I
could not resolve three issues for which I am requesting your help.

1) For some of the levels of x (), the values of y () with respect to
fill () are not in the correct segment of the bar (I can send you the
plot that I have produced and the data set that I have used, if
needed).

2) The opts () element “axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 16,
vjust=2,face = "bold")” did not produce the desired results. I could
not figure out why the ylab () is not bold in the plot.

3) The graph, which I have produced, is based on one of the eight
subsets of the main data set. May I request tips to write a function
with two arguments [datasets, levels of fill ()] that would produce
plots for 8 subsets of data in a single application?

Thanks in advance,

Pradip Muhuri




###### Below is the code for one subset

setwd ("C:/Documents and Settings/pradip.muhuri/My Documents")
library (ggplot2)

load("dfdescript.rdata")

# create 8 subsets of data
pop_mar <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="mar")
pop_edu <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="edu")
pop_inc <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="inc")
pop_ins <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="ins")
pop_emp <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="emp")
pop_fsp <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="fsp")
pop_pua <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="pua")
pop_wel <- subset(dfdescript,flag=="wel")

# The following code is used to plot geom_bar (the percent
distribution (y) with respect to
# the fill () factor for each level of x() using the "pop_mar" data
subset created above


pop_mar$race <- ordered (factor(pop_mar$race,levels=c
(5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
labels=c("Asian","Black","HI/
OPI","Hispanic","White",
"Multi Race","AI/AN")))

pop_mar$fill_var <- ordered (factor(pop_mar$fill_var, levels=c
(2,3,1),
labels=c("Never Married","Div/Wid/Sep",
"Married")))

p <- ggplot(pop_mar, aes(x=race, y=percentage, fill=fill_var))+
geom_bar(stat="identity")+
geom_text(aes(label=percentage,
y=percentage, angle=90, vjust =0,
face="bold")) +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("Married"="red",
"Never
Married"="skyblue",
"Div/Wid/Sep"=
"yellow"))+
coord_flip()+
xlab (" ") +
ylab("Percentage")+
labs (fill=" ")+


opts(legend.position="bottom",legend.direction="horizontal",
legend.text = theme_text(colour="black", size =
16, face = "bold"),
panel.grid.major=theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(),
title="Marital Status by Race/Ethnicity",
axis.text.y=theme_text(size=16, hjust=1,
face="bold"),
axis.text.x=theme_text(size=16, hjust=1,
face="bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 16, vjust=2,face
= "bold"),
panel.background=theme_rect(),
plot.title = theme_text(size=24, face="bold")
)

print (p)
ggsave(file="marital.png", width=7, height=7)

http://gist.github.com/270442

theme_bw() +
geom_bar(aes(fill = Admit), stat = 'identity') +
facet_wrap(~ Dept) +

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: GEOM_BAR (Stacked Bar)
parts:
Hi:

Thank you for the reproducible example. Hopefully the code below will be of use.

I was hoping to say that one could write a single plot function and
then apply it across all subsets of the data in one shot, but after
looking at the data briefly, it doesn't make sense to do so since the
subsets are qualitatively different and the number of levels of
fill_var change across the different data subsets. Evidently the
various subsets (flag) are qualitatively different tables. It appears
that you'll have to do some work by hand to arrange the sub-data
frames such that they can be called within the plot function defined
below. In particular, you probably want to make the plot title an
argument of the function, which I show below.

I'll illustrate how I modified the data and plot code for the first
subset and leave the rest to you. Since race appears to be consistent
throughout the data, you may want to do this first: By doing this up
front, you won't have to repeat it for each data subset.

# library('ggplot2')
# library('plyr')
dfdescript <- within(dfdescript, {
race <- factor(race, levels=c (5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
labels=c('Asian', 'Black', 'HI/OPI', 'Hispanic',
'White', 'Multi Race', 'AI/AN')) } )

# Step 1: Define the data subset and redefine race and fill_var to be factors.

pmar <- subset(dfdescript, flag == 'mar')
pmar <- within(pmar, {
# race <- factor(race, levels=c (5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
# labels=c('Asian', 'Black', 'HI/OPI', 'Hispanic',
# 'White', 'Multi Race', 'AI/AN'))
fill_var <- factor(fill_var, levels = c(2, 3, 1),
labels=c('Never
Married','Div/Wid/Sep', 'Married'))
} )
# Sort data by race and fill_var [uses arrange() from plyr]
pmar <- arrange(pmar, race, fill_var)
# Cumulate the percentages to use as a plotting position in the plot function
pmar <- ddply(pmar, .(race), transform, cpct = cumsum(percentage))
# Generate a plot title
martitle <- 'Marital Status by Race/Ethnicity'

plotfun <- function(dd, plotTitle, outFile)
{
print(ggplot(pmar, aes(x = race, y = percentage, fill = fill_var)) +
geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
geom_text(aes(y = cpct - 4, label = percentage), size = 5) +

scale_fill_manual(values=c('Married'='red',
'Never Married'='skyblue',

'Div/Wid/Sep'= 'yellow')) +
coord_flip()+
labs (x = "", y = "Percentage", fill=" ") +

opts(legend.position="bottom",
legend.direction="horizontal",
legend.text = theme_text(colour="black", size = 16,

face = "bold"),
panel.grid.major=theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(),
title=plotTitle,
axis.text.y=theme_text(size=16, hjust=1, face="bold"),

axis.text.x=theme_text(size=16, face="bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),

# panel.background=theme_rect(),
plot.title = theme_text(size=24, face="bold")
)

)
ggsave(outFile)
}

plotfun(pmar, martitle, 'mar.png')

In plotfun, I offset the cumulative percentages by -4; it appears to
be a value that works for all the table subsets and keeps the
percentages from abutting the boundaries of the stacked bars. I think
you should do something with the percentage label, but I don't have
any firm recommendations. The label in the current version of the plot
function is neither bold nor enlarged and looks out of place IMO.

You should just be able to redefine the levels of fill_var for each
subset table and then call plotfun() with a suitable main title and
output file name. If you don't want to see the plot on-screen, make
this the last line of plotfun():

invisible()

HTH,
Dennis

Hi:

Thank you for the reproducible example. Hopefully the code below will be of use.

I was hoping to say that one could write a single plot function and
then apply it across all subsets of the data in one shot, but after
looking at the data briefly, it doesn't make sense to do so since the
subsets are qualitatively different and the number of levels of
fill_var change across the different data subsets. Evidently the
various subsets (flag) are qualitatively different tables. It appears
that you'll have to do some work by hand to arrange the sub-data
frames such that they can be called within the plot function defined
below. In particular, you probably want to make the plot title an
argument of the function, which I show below.

I'll illustrate how I modified the data and plot code for the first
subset and leave the rest to you. Since race appears to be consistent
throughout the data, you may want to do this first: By doing this up
front, you won't have to repeat it for each data subset.

# library('ggplot2')
# library('plyr')
dfdescript <- within(dfdescript, {
race <- factor(race, levels=c (5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
labels=c('Asian', 'Black', 'HI/OPI', 'Hispanic',
'White', 'Multi Race', 'AI/AN')) } )

# Step 1: Define the data subset and redefine race and fill_var to be factors.

pmar <- subset(dfdescript, flag == 'mar')
pmar <- within(pmar, {
# race <- factor(race, levels=c (5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
# labels=c('Asian', 'Black', 'HI/OPI', 'Hispanic',
# 'White', 'Multi Race', 'AI/AN'))
fill_var <- factor(fill_var, levels = c(2, 3, 1),
labels=c('Never
Married','Div/Wid/Sep', 'Married'))
} )
# Sort data by race and fill_var [uses arrange() from plyr]
pmar <- arrange(pmar, race, fill_var)
# Cumulate the percentages to use as a plotting position in the plot function
pmar <- ddply(pmar, .(race), transform, cpct = cumsum(percentage))
# Generate a plot title
martitle <- 'Marital Status by Race/Ethnicity'

plotfun <- function(dd, plotTitle, outFile)
{
print(ggplot(pmar, aes(x = race, y = percentage, fill = fill_var)) +
geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
geom_text(aes(y = cpct - 4, label = percentage), size = 5) +
scale_fill_manual(values=c('Married'='red',
'Never Married'='skyblue',
'Div/Wid/Sep'= 'yellow')) +
coord_flip()+
labs (x = "", y = "Percentage", fill=" ") +
opts(legend.position="bottom",
legend.direction="horizontal",
legend.text = theme_text(colour="black", size = 16,
face = "bold"),
panel.grid.major=theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(),
title=plotTitle,
axis.text.y=theme_text(size=16, hjust=1, face="bold"),
axis.text.x=theme_text(size=16, face="bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
# panel.background=theme_rect(),
plot.title = theme_text(size=24, face="bold")
)
)
ggsave(outFile)
}

plotfun(pmar, martitle, 'mar.png')

In plotfun, I offset the cumulative percentages by -4; it appears to
be a value that works for all the table subsets and keeps the
percentages from abutting the boundaries of the stacked bars. I think
you should do something with the percentage label, but I don't have
any firm recommendations. The label in the current version of the plot
function is neither bold nor enlarged and looks out of place IMO.

You should just be able to redefine the levels of fill_var for each
subset table and then call plotfun() with a suitable main title and
output file name. If you don't want to see the plot on-screen, make
this the last line of plotfun():

invisible()

HTH,
Dennis

header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
closeAllConnections()
plotTitle <- "TfL Learning Environment"

# Use the new mutate() function, a faster version of transform()
# cfrq computes cumulative percent frequencies by
# ext.obs/comp combinations
tab3.1m <- mutate(tab3.1, Var1 = factor(Var1, levels = 1:4),
cfrq = ave(Freq, list(ext.obs, comp), FUN =
cumsum))

ggplot(tab3.1m, aes(x = ext.obs, y = Freq, fill = Var1)) +

geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
labs (x = "", y = "Percentage", fill=" ") +

scale_fill_brewer(name="Rating", palette="BrBG",
breaks = rev(levels(tab3.1m$Var1))) +
geom_text(aes(y = cfrq - 1,

label=paste(round(Freq, 1), "%", sep='')),
size=3) +

facet_grid(. ~ comp) +
opts(title = plotTitle)

HTH,
Dennis

On Tue, 2011-08-30 at 16:50 -0700, Dennis Murphy wrote:
> plotTitle <- "TfL Learning Environment"
>
> # Use the new mutate() function, a faster version of transform()
> # cfrq computes cumulative percent frequencies by
> # ext.obs/comp combinations
> tab3.1m <- mutate(tab3.1, Var1 = factor(Var1, levels = 1:4),
> cfrq = ave(Freq, list(ext.obs, comp), FUN =
> cumsum))
>
> ggplot(tab3.1m, aes(x = ext.obs, y = Freq, fill = Var1)) +
> geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
> labs (x = "", y = "Percentage", fill=" ") +
> scale_fill_brewer(name="Rating", palette="BrBG",
> breaks = rev(levels(tab3.1m$Var1))) +
> geom_text(aes(y = cfrq - 1,
> label=paste(round(Freq, 1), "%", sep='')),
> size=3) +
> facet_grid(. ~ comp) +
> opts(title = plotTitle)

Dennis, That's awesome. I didn't even ask about locating the text
annotations, and did a cumbersome thing with a for() loop, but your
solution is far more elegant. Thanks!!
